B: Hello! Hi, can you hear me okay?
A: Yes. I thought last one was finished, then another one comes.
B: Oh, sorry! I think it's four rounds. I'm Agnieszka, I'm in Basingstoke.
A: Shahida. Ilford.
B: Nice to meet you. How has it been, the calls?
A: Ok. Everybody very polite. The mechanic, he doesn't eat properly.
B: Oh, Lee! He helped me with my car, actually. A noise in the front. He said it's a drop link, I wrote it down.
A: Good. Free advice, that's the best kind.
B: Exactly! Normally the garage, they charge you just to look.
A: Everything costs now. You do your shopping where?
B: Aldi, mostly. And there is Polish shop on the high street, for bread, sausage, things from home. But they keep running out of the good bread, it's so annoying.
A: New Lidl near me, very cheap. Fruit, veg, good price. Meat I don't buy there, only from my butcher.
B: Yes, I understand, you have your butcher you trust. My mum is the same in Rzeszów, thirty years the same man.
A: Correct. Same man, he knows me, he doesn't give me rubbish.
B: Do you cook every day?
A: Every day. Roti fresh. Daal, karahi. My grandchildren, two days a week, I feed them.
B: Oh, that's lovely. I have a daughter, Zosia, she's nine. I cook most evenings, but simple. Pasta bake, soup. When my mum visits, we make pierogi together, hundreds, and I freeze them.
A: Pierogi, what is it?
B: Sort of dumplings. Dough, and inside potato and cheese, or cabbage, or meat. You boil them, then fry with onion.
A: Like samosa, but boiled. Ok. Freezing is clever. I also freeze, parathas, keema, ready for the week.
B: Yes! Then on a busy day, you have something proper, you know?
A: Better than takeaway. You live in house or flat?
B: House, a semi. We bought in 2015, on a newer estate. Still mortgage, of course.
A: We finished ours long time ago. Own outright. My husband wanted new car, I said no, house first.
B: That's very wise. That's what I want also, security. More than anything, really, after Brexit and everything. Sorry, that's a big topic.
A: Hm. People say things. You have your house, your job, your passport. Then they can say what they like.
B: Yes. That's true. I got citizenship in 2019, for that reason. Peace of mind.
A: Good. Paper is important. That's it.
B: I bake also, cheesecake, for work. Do you bake?
A: No. Diabetes. Doctor says no sugar, so I don't make sweet things now. Only for Eid.
B: Oh, sorry. Only for Eid is fair, I think.
A: Acha. Time is finishing, I think.
